overview: This file consists of a one-page list of papers filed under “Agriculture - Formosa (Taiwan).” It indexes two reports: a Shanghai communication transmitting Agricultural Attaché Owen L. Dawson’s memorandum on conditions observed during an official trip to Taiwan, chiefly concerning agriculture, and a Taihoku report stating that Taiwan’s 1940 rice harvests were among the poorest in years and that sugar production was also expected to be low. The underlying reports themselves are not present in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Agriculture—Formosa (Taiwan)
subfiles.about: A file index records two communications concerning general agricultural conditions and poor rice and sugar production in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a Shanghai communication numbered 3128, associated with Butrick, which transmitted a May 7 memorandum by Agricultural Attaché Owen L. Dawson on conditions encountered during an official trip to Taiwan, chiefly agricultural matters. It also lists Taihoku report no. 123, associated with Werner, dated October 4, reporting that Taiwan’s first and second rice crops of 1940 were the poorest in years and predicting low sugar production. The index supplies related decimal-file references for the latter report, but the two indexed documents are not reproduced in the supplied text.

interest: Although only an index survives in the supplied OCR, it identifies two potentially valuable contemporary assessments of Taiwan’s colonial agricultural economy. Of particular interest is the October report connecting poor first and second rice crops with an anticipated decline in sugar output in 1940. The sheet also preserves document numbers, responsible officers, routing codes, and related decimal-file references that could help a historian locate the missing reports elsewhere in Record Group 59.
